title: Why Drainage Pipes Suffer Chronic Blockages: Pipe Sag & Slugging
description: Chronic drain clogs are often caused by a belly or sag in the drainage line rather than routine organic buildup. When a horizontal drain pipe loses its consistent slope, water settles in the low point, creating a standing pool. Solid waste and toilet paper slow down upon entering this standing water, losing momentum and settling at the bottom. Over time, these solids accumulate into persistent blockages. Simply cabling or snaking the line provides only temporary relief because the structural dip remains. Resolving this issue requires identifying the bellied section with a sewer inspection camera and properly resetting the pipe's support and slope according to local code requirements.

Simply cabling or snaking the line provides only temporary relief because the structural dip remains. Resolving this issue requires identifying the bellied section with a sewer inspection camera and properly resetting the pipe's support and slope according to local code requirements.
